items.root_cause: Nothing tells a scheduled task that the daily chain is in flight, so five scheduled pulls of the production checkout run on a clock that assumes the chain has finished (the chain ran past 09:45 on 7 of the 26 days on disk: 09-09, 09-12, 09-20, 09-23, 09-24, 09-26, 09-27). A pull that brings an upstream change to commodities.json, known-wrong.json, board-price-overrides.json or product-urls.json after guards moves the verdict fingerprint and withholds a board guards passed. Separately, sessions commit in the production checkout mid-run (09-20, proven), which Stage 2 W2.1 of the ruled dedicated-checkout plan already owns.

root_fix.what: One sync entry point for every scheduled pull of the production checkout, which SKIPS the pull while a capture-run is in flight, read lock-free from the run status record; the four SKILL prompts and bakers-daily-scan.ps1 call it instead of a bare 'git pull --rebase --autostash'.
root_fix.exact_change: 1) ops/sync-production-checkout.ps1 [-Repo C:/Codex/ThriftyCrew] [-StatusFile <repo>/grocery/out/logs/capture-run-status.json] [-SelfTest]: Test-TcCaptureRunInFlight reads the status json ONCE (og-53: one sample of one record survives every read anomaly), and returns in-flight when ANY kind (daily, ad) has date = today, a stage that is not terminal (read the terminal set from capture-run.ps1's Write-RunStatus call sites; at least complete, failed and skipped-locked; a switch on stage carries a default that treats an unknown stage as IN FLIGHT, fail closed, og-16), and a pid that is alive. In flight -> print 'SYNC-SKIPPED capture-run <kind> in stage <stage> (pid <n>, started <t>) - the production checkout is not pulled while the chain runs' and exit 0. Otherwise run 'git -C <repo> pull --rebase --autostash origin main' through Invoke-Native (grocery/native-lib.ps1, og-04), print its last line, exit its rc. Unreadable or absent status file -> pull as today and say 'status unreadable, pulling' (degrade to the day before, never to a refusal). Last line 'SYNC-PRODUCTION-CHECKOUT-COMPLETE outcome=<skipped|pulled|failed>'. DO NOT take Global\tc-capture-run: capture-run waits only 60 s (capture-run.ps1:605) so a sync holding it across a slow network pull makes the chain skip its day, and a WaitOne on an abandoned mutex consumes the abandoned state capture-run.ps1:610 relies on to detect an orphaned child. Self-contained on purpose, not a function in lib/checkout-sync.ps1: that lib is in the chain's derived set, so extending it would force a chain rehearsal for a change the chain never runs; cost is one small script, 0 seconds per push beyond its self-test. 2) grocery/bakers-daily-scan.ps1:78: replace the bare git pull (the shape test-native-stderr-eap.ps1:425 already names) with a call to the script, keeping its existing log and its could-not-restore page. 3) The four SKILL prompts: replace the 'git -C C:\Codex\ThriftyCrew pull --rebase --autostash origin main' command with 'powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File C:\Codex\ThriftyCrew\ops\sync-production-checkout.ps1' and one sentence: 'SYNC-SKIPPED means the daily chain is running: carry on with the checkout as it is'. Edit the live copy AND the ops/prompt-backup mirror in the same change, then run ops/audit-prompt-backup.ps1.

items.root_cause: Get-TcArtifactProducers already accepts DATAFLOW for roots (a variable assigned the artifact's leaf and written elsewhere in the file, :125-133) but not for EDGES: it follows a script only when its literal name sits on the invoking line. So every script a producer launches through a variable holding a literal name is outside the set (46 such invocations today), and whatever that script writes or loads can change mid-run without a stale-artifact page. The residual's two named classes measured differently from how they were written: parameter-passed writers 0 real instances among invocation lines, and computed names 8 sites of which 2 are in never-walked hubs.

root_fix.what: Dataflow edges, the same rule the dataflow roots already use: inside a walked script, a line that invokes $<var> adds the literal script leaf that the same script assigns to $<var>.
root_fix.exact_change: In Get-TcArtifactProducers' closure loop (:138-164), before the per-line name scan: build one map per script, $<var> (lower-cased) -> the literal *.ps1/*.js leaf on a line '^\s*\$<var>\s*=' (last assignment wins, as the prototype did). Then for each code line matching '(-File\s+|Invoke-NativeScript\s+(-\w+\s+)?|&\s*|\.\s+)\$<var>\b' where the map holds <var>, add the leaf to BOTH $invNamed and $allNamed (so the hub count at :158 still sees it). $PSCommandPath and $self-style self re-invocations never enter the map (no literal leaf). Update the header's SCOPE OF A CLEAN ANSWER line: unsound now only for a script path assembled at run time or passed in as a parameter, and for an artifact path assembled in another function, and say that its 2026-09-28 measure was 8 such invocation sites, 2 inside hubs. BEFORE landing, read each of the 15 distinct additions' invoking line in the producer that reaches it and say in the commit which are self-test-only invocations (hold-recipe, selftest-names-lib, audit-blocker-lib and hunt-run are the suspects): d70062's founding bug was over-inclusion that paged falsely, so if a self-test-only edge would add a false page, skip lines inside a '$SelfTest' block the same way the comment strip skips doc text, and re-measure.
